1#main: Who is obligated in pidyon haben, when it is fit for redemption, and all its laws. In it are 31 seifim. It is a positive mitzvah for every man of Israel to redeem his son who is a firstborn to his mother—the Israelite woman—with five selaim, which are 120 ma'ot, which are thirty drachma of refined silver. {See above siman 294 how much a ma'ah is; and some say the five selaim are approximately two Rhenish gold coins, which are two Polish gold coins (Piskei Maharai siman 48).}
2#main: A woman is not obligated to redeem her son (Rambam, chapter 11 of Laws of Firstborn, halachah 2).
3#main: These five selaim he gives to the kohen in silver or in the equivalent of silver in whatever item he wishes, except for land, slaves, and promissory notes; and if he redeemed him with them, he is not redeemed.
4#main: If he wrote to the kohen that he owes him five selaim on account of his son's redemption, he is obligated to give them to him, but his son is not redeemed (Tur in the name of the Geonim). If he said to the kohen that he will give him to redeem his son, it is forbidden to retract; however, if he retracted, it is a retraction (Mordechai, end of Kol HaGet). (And see above siman 264.)
5#main: If he gave him an item that is not worth five selaim in the marketplace, and the kohen accepted it for five selaim—behold his son is redeemed (Rambam there)—provided it is worth five selaim to any person.
6#main: If he gave him an item for his son's redemption without specification—if it is worth five selaim, even though they did not appraise it initially, his son is redeemed. {Rama: And if it is not worth it, his son is not redeemed (Tur). And if the kohen wishes to keep the item, he need not return it to him, and he completes for him up to five selaim (Maharil).}
7#main: If he gave five selaim, even to ten kohanim, whether at once or one after another—his son is redeemed.
8#main: If the kohen wished to return the redemption to him, he may. But he should not give to the kohen on condition that he return it to him; and if he did so, and the kohen returned it to him—and the kohen's intent was initially not to accept it on condition to return (as implied in Beit Yosef)—his son is not redeemed until he resolves in his heart to give him a complete gift; and if the kohen wished afterward to return, he may return. And a kohen should not be accustomed to return to everyone, lest other kohanim not receive their pidyon habein from anyone; but to the poor he may return each time. And all the more so he should not accept them on condition to return. Nevertheless, if he transgressed and accepted them and explained that he gives on condition to return—the son is redeemed, for a gift on condition to return is called a gift. (And specifically when he said on condition to return; but if he said, "Here are five selaim for you and return them to me," it is not a gift and his son is not redeemed (Rashba siman 498 and 359).)}
9#main: If he separated five selaim for his son's redemption and they were lost, he is liable for them until they reach the kohen's hand.
10#main: At the time he gives the redemption to the kohen, he blesses "Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning the redemption of the son," and repeats and blesses shehecheyanu, and afterward gives the redemption to the kohen. And if he redeems himself, he blesses "Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to redeem the firstborn," and blesses shehecheyanu (Rambam there, halachah 5). {Rama: And some say that even one who redeems himself blesses on the redemption of the firstborn, and so is the custom (Tur and Rivash siman 131). And see above siman 265: some bring the firstborn before the kohen and inform him that he is a firstborn, opener of the womb, and the kohen asks him, "Which do you prefer—your firstborn son or the five selaim that you are obligated to redeem him with?" And the father says, "My firstborn son," and here are five selaim for his redemption; and while giving him the money he blesses the blessings mentioned (Tur and Rosh in the name of the Geonim). And so is the custom in these lands when the father is with the son; but if he is not with him, he redeems him anyway, only telling the kohen that he has a firstborn to redeem, and he says, "Which do you prefer," etc. (so in Hagahos Mordechai, end of HaIshah, and so Beit Yosef in the name of Semak). And if the father wished to leave the son to the kohen, he does not leave him—he must redeem him (Piskei Maharai siman 135). And some wrote that the custom is to make a meal at the time of redemption (there in Hagahos Mordechai, Maharil, and Terumat HaDeshen siman 269). And if there is wine in the city, the kohen blesses on wine immediately after the redemption (Maharil). And so is the practice now in order to publicize the matter; and they do not practice blessing "the joy in His dwelling" (Abudraham). And the father cannot redeem through an agent; and likewise bet din does not redeem him without the father (Rivash siman 131).}
11#main: The firstborn is not fit for redemption until thirty days have passed over him; and after thirty days he redeems him immediately, so as not to delay the mitzvah. And if the thirty-first day occurs on Shabbat, they do not redeem him on Shabbat but wait until Sunday. {Some say one should not perform pidyon haben on chol hamoed (Mahariu in the name of Sefer HaMitzvot Mitzurak); and some permit (Tosafot, first chapter of Moed Katan). And so is the essential ruling.}
12#main: If the son died within thirty days—even on the thirtieth day—and likewise if he became a treifah before thirty days passed over him, he is not obligated in redemption; and even if he preceded and gave the redemption to the kohen, he returns it to him. {If he died after thirty days, he must redeem him (Tur) and bless on the redemption; but he does not bless shehecheyanu (logical opinion, and so Maharik, end of root 49).}
13#main: One who redeemed his son within thirty days—if he said to him "from now," his son is not redeemed; and if he said "after thirty days," his son is redeemed even though the money does not exist after thirty days. {Rama: And some say if the money does not exist, or he returned it to the father within thirty, even b'dieved his son is not redeemed (Maharai in Terumat HaDeshen siman 264 and in his writings siman 234). And it is good to be stringent and redeem again.} One who is in doubt whether he is obligated in redemption is exempt, for the burden of proof is on the one who extracts from his fellow.
14#main: If the father died within thirty days, the son is presumed not redeemed until he brings proof that his father redeemed him; and if the father died after thirty days, he is presumed redeemed until they inform him that he commanded at the time of death and said he was not redeemed.
15#main: If the father transgressed and did not redeem his son, when he grows up he is obligated to redeem himself. {And some wrote that they write for him on a silver tag that he is not redeemed and hang it on his neck so he knows to redeem himself when he grows (Maharil).} If he was to redeem himself and his son to redeem—he redeems himself first and afterward redeems his son; and if he has only enough for one redemption, he redeems himself.
16#main: If he has no free property for redemption, the kohen does not collect from liened property, even though the redemption debt preceded the creditor's debt.
17#main: Pidyon haben depends only on peter rechem—for if he is not a firstborn to the mother, even though he is a firstborn to the father, he is not obligated in redemption. And if he has several wives and has a firstborn from each one, he is obligated to redeem all of them.
18#main: Kohanim and Levites are exempt from pidyon haben; and even a kohenet or leviah married to an Israelite—the son is not obligated in redemption, for the matter does not depend on the father but on the mother, as it says "opener of the womb in Israel." And if she conceived from a gentile—the son of the leviah is exempt from redemption, and the son of the kohenet is obligated in redemption, for his mother was profaned from the priesthood through relations with the gentile. {Rama: And if she says she conceived from an Israelite and the Israelite denies her and says she conceived from a gentile—the son is exempt from redemption (Terumat HaDeshen siman 264).}
19#main: A kohen who had a mamzer son—if the father died within thirty days, the son is obligated to redeem himself, for the father did not acquire his redemption; and if the father died after thirty days, the father already acquired his redemption and his son inherits it from him; therefore he separates the redemption and sets it aside for himself.
20#main: A maidservant who was freed and a female convert who converted while pregnant and gave birth—even though their conception was not in holiness, since he was born in holiness he is obligated, as it says "opener of the womb in Israel"—and behold his womb was opened in Israel. It is unknown whether before she converted or after she converted the conception.
21#main: A female convert and a maidservant who gave birth and afterward converted and were freed and afterward gave birth—they are exempt, for this is not peter rechem.
22#main: An eight-month fetus whose head emerged and he lived, and he returned and died; or a nine-month fetus whose head emerged even after death, and afterward his brother emerged and she bore a viable child—this is not peter rechem, for he was released through the head of the first. And once his pedachat was released, it releases what comes after him. And likewise one who miscarries in the form of a beast, wild animal, or bird whose half-face resembles human form, or a sandal, or a placenta, or an embroidered fetus (meaning: a piece of flesh like the form of a sandal; and placenta: the pouch in which the fetus lies; and embroidered fetus: a piece of flesh in which there is human form—Aruch)—or the child emerged cut limb by limb—one born after any of these is not peter rechem (Tur's wording).
23#main: An eight-month fetus whose head emerged dead; and one who miscarries a fetus full of blood, or full of water, or full of colors; and one who miscarries in the form of fish and grasshoppers and creeping things; and one who miscarries on the fortieth day—one born after all these is a firstborn for redemption. {And as long as his limbs are not formed, it does not release what comes after him—and even at this time we rely on this (Maharik, root 143).}
24#main: A caesarean birth and one born after him in the usual way—both are exempt: the first because he did not emerge from the womb, and the second because another preceded him.
25#main: One whose wife had not previously given birth and she bore a male and a female and it is unknown which of them emerged first—there is nothing here for the kohen. If she bore two males—even though it is unknown which is the firstborn—he gives five selaim to the kohen. If one of them died within thirty days, he is exempt, lest the firstborn died; and the burden of proof is on the one who extracts from his fellow.
26#main: If the father died before he redeemed them—whether he died within thirty or after thirty—and the sons survive, they give five selaim between them, even if they already divided the property.
27#main: Two wives who had not previously given birth and bore two males—he gives ten selaim to the kohen. If one of them died within thirty days: if he gave to one kohen, he returns five selaim to him; and if he gave to two kohanim, he cannot extract from them, for he did not apply this redemption to this son and to that son, and each will say, "I hold for the living one." If they bore a male and a female, or two males and a female—he gives five selaim to the kohen. And if one of the males died within thirty days, he gives nothing to the kohen. If they bore two females and a male, or two males and two females, and it is unknown which was born first—there is nothing here for the kohen, for I say a female was born first and afterward a male (Tur's wording).
28#main: Two wives, one of whom had previously given birth and one had not, and they bore two males and they became mixed—he gives five selaim to the kohen. And if one of them died within thirty days, there is nothing here for the kohen. And if the father died, they give five selaim between them. Male and female, or two males and a female—there is nothing here for the kohen.
29#main: Two women of two men who had not previously given birth and bore two males and they became mixed—this one gives five selaim and that one gives five selaim. If they gave and afterward one of the sons died within thirty days: if they gave to two kohanim, they cannot extract from their hands; and if they gave to one kohen, one of them writes authorization to his fellow and this one goes with authorization and extracts five selaim from the kohen. And if they bore a male and a female and it is unknown which bore the male and which bore the female; or if they bore two males and they became mixed and one of them died—the fathers are exempt and the living son is obligated to redeem himself.
30#main: And likewise a pregnant woman who did not wait three months after her husband and remarried and bore a male—there is doubt whether he is a nine-month child of the first or a seven-month child of the second; the fathers are exempt and the son is obligated to redeem himself. And if they bore two females and a male, or two males and two females—there is nothing here for the kohen.
31#main: Two women of two men, one of whom had previously given birth and one had not, and they bore two males—he whose wife had not previously given birth gives five selaim to the kohen. Male and female, or two males and a female—there is nothing here for the kohen.
